column7: G1 (FUZZ-GAPS) follow-up to login-rate-limit-reserve-first-001/PR #1981: that fix's own PR body flagged ConsumeSetup and BeginWebAuthnPasswordlessLogin as "explicitly out of scope" -- both shared checkLoginRateLimit's gate but never called reserveLoginAttempt at all, even pre-#1981, so unlike their six siblings neither ever contributed to the shared per-IP login-attempt budget and either could be hammered without limit, defeating the rate limiter as a brute-force/DoS throttle on those two endpoints specifically. Confirmed by FuzzLoginThrottleConcurrency (login_throttle_fuzz_test.go), a deterministic controlled-interleaving harness driving all 8 budget-sharing endpoints against a real storage-backed KeyorixCore and checking ground-truth login_attempts row counts (never wall-clock timing). Fixed by adding the same reserveLoginAttempt call, in the same position (after the minimal well-formedness check, before the slow step), to both call sites. Red-before/green-after: reverting both new reserveLoginAttempt calls made 9 of the harness's 11 corpus entries fail with "BUDGET NOT RESERVED"; restoring them passed all 11.
